summary: Set 124 Session 3 propagated the machine/project claim to every live echo, then found and fixed two defects the spec had not anticipated -- one of them Critical, and created by this set's own Session 2. THE DOC PASS (as planned): README.md, docs/quick-start.md (both inventory rows -- local-overrides.yaml now names its retired transport.profile), AGENTS/CLAUDE/GEMINI.md, docs/planning/verify-type-resolution.md (a Set 124 amendment banner in the status preamble per L-064-8 rather than a rewrite, because it is a dated design record), docs/tutorials/adopt-dabbler.md, and docs/templates/consumer-bootstrap/getting-started.md.template, which had asserted the EXACT INVERSE of the operator's ruling; an already-committed consumer is now told to git rm --cached. DEFECT 1 (Critical, fixed): performCopilotSeatSetup still rendered transport.profile: copilot-cli into ai_router/local-overrides.yaml -- the key S2 made a HARD REFUSAL -- so a SUCCESSFUL 'Dabbler: Set Up Copilot Seat' handed the operator a project whose every load_config raised ValueError. Reproduced in a throwaway fixture before deciding anything, brought to the operator as an education-mode brief rather than fixed unilaterally (it expanded session scope), and journaled under goal-over-letter. The operator's constraint -- 'we can't break the Direct API option, but we need to support COPILOT_CLI' -- selected the fix: retarget the write to the ONE sanctioned entry point, spawning `<venvPython> -m ai_router.verify_type --set COPILOT_CLI --project-root <dir>` through the same scaffolded interpreter the catalog refresh uses, so there is exactly one writer of project-verify-type.txt. Direct API is untouched by construction: an 'api' pick was always a no-op. The retired YAML-render machinery (locateTransportProfile / hasTopLevelTransportBlock / renderTransportProfile / RenderProfileResult) is deleted, readTransportProfile became readProjectVerifyType, and outcome kind config-write-failed became verify-type-write-failed. DEFECT 2 (Major, fixed), found BY the cold-start walk the spec required: write_project_verify_type embeds a header reading 'Gitignored on purpose', and nothing gitignored it -- the documented first run left the answer untracked and COMMITTABLE (git check-ignore exit 1). The writer now calls a new ensure_gitignored() BEFORE writing the file, so there is no window in which the answer exists un-ignored; is_gitignored_by() is conservative in the safe direction and never counts comments or '!' re-includes. That made the .gitignore guarantee this session had JUST added to the extension a second implementation of one fact, so it was deleted (with writeFileAtomically, whose last caller it was) and the extension inherits the guarantee through the spawn. VERIFICATION found the seam left by that removal (round 1, Major, accepted): the guarantee moved but its failure signal did not, so an unwritable .gitignore would have produced a toast claiming the file was gitignored when it was not. The extension now RELAYS the writer's own stderr warning rather than re-deriving anything, matched line-anchored on 'WARNING: ' so Python's own RuntimeWarning noise -- present on every invocation -- cannot be mistaken for it. Round 3 remediation-review: VERIFIED, fix accepted. THE COLD START itself passed end to end from an empty folder plus bare git init: branch 3 fired (exit 3) naming the gitignore rationale, --set COPILOT_CLI resolved the project on branch 1 (exit 0), and the re-walk showed check-ignore claiming the file with git status clean of it. Suites: pytest 4006 passed / 9 skipped; Playwright 31 passed; mocha 1462 passing / 2 pending -- all re-run after the last code change. CHECKLIST DISCLOSURE: three verification-round transitions left a record with no checklist post before the next one happened. The gate is advisory and no waiver is claimed here, because an operator attestation is not the orchestrator's to author; the misses are disclosed instead.
